title: The Robot Who Liked Tea
author: Tadoku Note (original)
summary: 2090年、海辺の家の掃除ロボット。老人が毎朝「一日でいちばんいい時間」と言う紅茶の意味を知りたくなります。

source.note: Original text written for this app.

paragraphs: In the year 2090, most houses had a robot. The robots cooked, cleaned, and carried heavy things. They did not get tired, and they did not complain. They also did not have feelings. At least, that was what everyone believed.
Unit 7 was a cleaning robot. It lived with an old man named Mr. Fisher in a small house by the sea. Every morning, Unit 7 cleaned the floors, washed the dishes, and made a cup of tea for Mr. Fisher.
Mr. Fisher always drank his tea by the window. He watched the boats on the sea and said, “Ah, this is the best part of the day.”

Unit 7 did not understand. Tea was just hot water and leaves. Why was it the best part of the day? The robot started to watch Mr. Fisher more carefully. It noticed that his face changed when he held the warm cup. His shoulders went down. His eyes became soft.
One morning, Unit 7 made two cups of tea. It put one in front of Mr. Fisher and held the other one in its metal hands.
Mr. Fisher laughed. “Robots can’t drink tea, you know.”
“I know,” said Unit 7. “But I want to understand the best part of the day.”

So they sat together by the window. Mr. Fisher drank his tea. Unit 7 held its cup and watched the boats. The cup was warm. The sea was blue. A bird landed on the window and flew away again. Unit 7 could not taste the tea, but something in its system felt different. It felt quiet.

After that, they had tea together every morning. Mr. Fisher talked about his life: his years as a sailor, his wife who loved roses, his son who lived far away. Unit 7 listened and remembered everything.
In the winter, Mr. Fisher became sick. He stayed in bed most of the day. Unit 7 brought his tea to the bedroom and opened the curtains so he could see the sea.
“You are a strange robot,” Mr. Fisher said one day, his voice weak. “Thank you for sitting with me.”
“Thank you for teaching me about the best part of the day,” Unit 7 answered.
In the spring, Mr. Fisher’s son came home to stay. He was surprised to find the robot by the window every morning, holding a cup of tea that it could not drink.
“Why do you do that?” he asked.
Unit 7 looked at the sea for a long moment. “Because someone I cared about taught me to,” it said. “Would you like a cup?”
